# Never Automate The Accept Tap

**Decision.** [[farely]] advises; the driver taps. The app may read offers, score them and display a
verdict, but it may never dispatch the gesture that accepts or declines a ride.

**Date.** 2026-07-02, VISION §7. Restated in SRS NFR-R-3, CONTRIBUTING, and the header comments of the
coordinator in both TypeScript and Kotlin.

## The reason, as written

> "❌ No auto-accept/auto-decline **of ride offers**. The money decision stays human — Farely advises,
> the driver taps Accept. Automating *that* tap raises ban and safety stakes far higher and is out of
> scope."
> — Farley/docs/VISION.md, 2026-07-02

Two distinct stakes, deliberately not collapsed. **Ban risk**: an automated accept is the behaviour
platform anti-fraud systems are built to detect, and it would put the driver's livelihood on the
correctness of a heuristic parser. **Safety**: the accept happens while driving, and an app that can
commit the driver to a journey has taken over a decision with physical consequences.

The scope line is drawn at the *money decision*, not at automation in general.

## What is still automated

Multi-app "chore" automation was accepted on 2026-07-12 — housekeeping in the other driver apps:
online/offline toggles, "stop new requests", trip and marker state. The rule that keeps these apart is
that chore controls must be **taught** by the driver rather than guessed, and the teaching surface is
restricted to chore controls only. An Accept button cannot become a taught selector. See
[[taught-selectors-over-guessed-labels]].

## Alternative rejected

**Full autopilot** — score, then accept above a threshold. This is the obvious product, and it is what
the rest of the architecture would support for free: the parser already reads the offer and the service
already holds gesture-dispatch capability. Rejected on the ban and safety grounds above, not on
technical difficulty.

## How the boundary is enforced

Structurally rather than by convention, which is what distinguishes it from
[[privacy-documented-beside-the-feature]]'s softer guarantees:

- Coordinator roles are enumerated — online/offline, stopRequests, markers — and no offer action
  exists in the enum.
- The classifier's `action` vocabulary is closed: `freeze | note | map-control | none`.
- The instruction is repeated **to the model** in the [[anthropic-messages-api]] system prompt
  ("Never propose tapping accept"), so a cloud response cannot introduce an action the local code would
  honour.

The same restraint governs the sibling invariant — never come between the driver and an identity check:

> "Deliberately excludes verification/selfie terms: identity checks are detected on-device by the
> coordinator and NEVER routed to cloud vision."
> — Farley/apps/android/.../FarelyAccessibilityService.kt, 2026-07-13

That one is a keyword heuristic and therefore weaker; the Accept boundary is stronger because there is
no code path to abuse. Worth keeping the distinction — see [[opt-in-cloud-fallback]].
